author: BBC News
description:
Last week, President Donald Trump barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news". After their reporters had their press passes revoked and were denied access to the building, the three outlets launched a joint legal challenge, arguing that the move was unconstitutional.

How unprecedented is this decision? And how does it compare with the treatment of journalists in other countries around the world?
 
Jason Rezaian, host of the Washington Post podcast Freedom Desk and the paper's former Tehran bureau chief, has a unique perspective on these questions. While reporting from Iran, he experienced restrictions on press freedom and was ultimately imprisoned by the regime. Since his release, he has become a prominent advocate for press freedom around the world.
 
He joins The Global Story’s Tristan Redman to discuss where President Trump's decision fits into a broader pattern in the relationship between political leaders and the media over recent

Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says an OpenAI agent "infiltrated" the country's healthcare portal in a hack that experts say is the first known case of its kind. The country's cybersecurity agency is launching an investigation into the incident, which OpenAI says it only detected two months after it happened. The breach is likely to heighten concerns about the inability of AI's developers to control the technology.

author: BBC News
description:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has branded a ban on fans being allowed to drink alcohol in the stands during men's football matches as "discrimination".
 
The prime minister told reporters that "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out", as he suggested a change could be trialled.
 
Laws are in place which prevent drinking in view of the pitch at stadiums for clubs in the top five tiers of men's football in England. Other sports do not face such a restriction.
 
The Football Supporters' Association said the "outdated" legislation should be reviewed, but police chiefs have warned against relaxing the law and would like to meet the PM to "explain the challenges".

An OpenAI agent has “infiltrated" part of the Australian government's healthcare scheme Medicare. Experts say it's the world's first known breach of a government system by rogue AI agents
 
It accessed a statistics portal in June, OpenAI became aware in August and told the Australian government in September, via email.
 
So - how can this happen? In this video, the BBC's Cyber Correspondent Joe Tidy explains.

author: BBC News
description:
US President Donald Trump has greeted his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping with a military flyover and 100ft (30m) red carpet to kick off their three-day summit in Washington.
 
In a rare move, Trump welcomed Xi's entourage at the airport as the US Air Force band marched on the tarmac and US and Chinese flags flew.
 
Trump and First Lady Melania Trump welcomed Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening in Maryland.
 
The high-stakes visit - Xi's first trip to Washington since 2015 - is expected to include closed-door meetings, a state dinner, and plenty to discuss, from AI, to the Iran war and Taiwan, and an extended trade truce.

author: BBC News
description:
A US judge had temporarily overturned bans placed on MS Now, CNN and Politico from the White House.
 
A District of Columbia court issued a temporary restraining order against the ban, meaning CNN, MS NOW and Politico must have their access restored for 14 days, after ruling the move "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".
 
The Trump administration defended the move in court, accusing the outlets of publishing false information and threatening national security - an argument the court rejected.

author: BBC News
description:
Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has disclosed that an artificial intelligence agent developed by US firm OpenAI "infiltrated" a statistics portal on an Australian government website.

The agent hacked a statistics portal containing private data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme, Medicare. Experts believe it is the world's first known AI breach of a government system.

OpenAI says it is not believed any patient records were accessed.
